summary: The root ذعن (dhEn) primarily means quick obedience, acknowledgment, and submission. It implies being tractable and humble, readily complying with what is due.
lane: 4 اذعن لَهُ ذ , (S, Msb, * K, &c.,) inf. n. إِذْعَانٌ , (Msb,) He was, or became, quick in obedience to him, or it: (K:) this is its [proper, or primary,] meaning, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, in the language of the Arabs: (TA:) and he acknowledged, or confessed, to him: (K:) and he was, or became, lowly, or humble, and abject, to him: (S, K:) and he was, or became, tractable, submissive, or manageable, to him; (S, * Msb, * K, TA;) and easy; (K, * TA;) not disobedient; (Msb;) as also , aor. ذَعَنَ , (K,) inf. n. ذَعَنٌ . (TA.) You say, اذعن لِى بِحَقِّى He obeyed me with respect to that [ right, or due, ] which I sought to obtain from him, and hastened to render it: and he acknowledged, or confessed, to me my right, or due, willingly, not against his will; as also أَمْعَنَ . (TA.) Some have used إِذْعَانٌ as meaning Perception, and understanding: but there is no foundation for this in the language of the Arabs; and its being tropical, as some of the sheykhs have endeavoured to show it to be, is improbable. (MF.)

headwords.def: ا عن لَهُ , (S, Msb, * K, &c.,) inf. n. إِ ْعَانٌ, (Msb,) He was, or became, quick in obedience to him, or it: (K:) this is its [proper, or primary,] meaning, accord. to Aboo-Is-hák, in the language of the Arabs: (TA:) and he acknowledged, or confessed, to him: (K:) and he was, or became, lowly, or humble, and abject, to him: (S, K:) and he was, or became, tractable, submissive, or manageable, to him; (S, * Msb, * K, TA;) and easy; (K, * TA;) not disobedient; (Msb;) as also, aor.

[act. part. n. of 4]. وَإِنْ يَكُنْ لَهُمُ ٱلْحَقُّ يَأْتُوا إِلَيْهِ مُ ْعِنِينَ, in the Kur [xxiv. 48], means [ But if the right be theirs, ] they come to him quickly obedient: (TA:) or [simply] obedient; not compelled against their will: (Fr, TA:) or acknowledging, or confessing, and lowly, or humble: or tractable, submissive, or manageable, and easy.
رَأَيْتُهُمْ مُ ْعَانِّينَ is a mistake for رايتهم مُ ْعَابِّينَ, meaning I saw them following one another, or doing so uninterruptedly. (K.)

headword_note: Lane organises by verb form and principal noun, not by every inflected form. A word with no headword entry falls back to the root meaning; nothing is inferred.
